functions.description: Split a physical quantity string such as '10.0 mol' or '27°C' into its numeric value and its unit.
inputs: the quantity string with value and unit

functions.description: Convert an amount of substance given with a unit (mol, mmol, kmol, umol, nmol) to moles.
Convert a volume given in a common unit (dm3, L, cm3, mL, m3) to cubic metres.
Convert a temperature given in Celsius, Fahrenheit, Rankine or kelvin to kelvin.
Apply the perfect gas law p = nRT/V in SI units with R = 8.314 J K-1 mol-1 to obtain the pressure in pascals.
Convert a pressure in pascals to atmospheres, bar, kilopascals and megapascals.
Cross-check the perfect gas pressure using R = 0.08206 dm3 atm K-1 mol-1 with volume in dm3 and compare it with the SI-derived pressure in atmospheres.
Predict the pressure exerted by a gas confined to a given volume at a given temperature using the perfect gas law, reporting it in pascals, megapascals and atmospheres.
inputs: the amount of gas with unit
the chemical formula of the gas with its phase
the volume of the gas with unit
the temperature of the gas with unit
the common name of the gas

entry_points.text: Suppose that ●1 ●2 is confined to ●3 at ●4. Predict the pressure exerted by the ●5 from the perfect gas.

params.description: the amount of gas with unit
params.validity_range: Positive amount of substance (> 0), typically in mol or mmol; must be convertible to moles.

params.description: the chemical formula of the gas with its phase
params.validity_range: Any gaseous chemical species; under the perfect gas model the identity does not affect the result.

params.description: the volume of the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Positive volume (> 0) in a recognizable unit such as dm3, L, cm3, mL or m3.

params.description: the temperature of the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Temperature above absolute zero (T > 0 K) after conversion to kelvin; given in °C, K or °F.

params.description: the common name of the gas
params.validity_range: Name consistent with the gas formula; descriptive only, does not affect the calculation.
